title: COUNT(column) skips NULLs
question: Has COUNT ever fooled you?
fact_source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-aggregate.html (count(*) = number of input rows; count("any") = rows where the input value is not null)

scenes.headline: Your COUNT is missing rows
scenes.voice: Your count says forty users, but the table has fifty rows?
scenes.caption: Your COUNT says 40 users, but the table has 50 rows?

scenes.headline: COUNT(column) skips NULLs
scenes.voice: Count of a column only counts rows where that value is not null. Ten users have no phone, so they vanish.
scenes.caption: COUNT of a column only counts rows where that value is not NULL. Ten users have no phone, so they vanish.

scenes.headline: Count rows with COUNT(*)
scenes.voice: To count rows, use count star. Keep count of a column only when you want the non-null values.
scenes.caption: To count rows, use COUNT(*). Keep COUNT of a column only when you want the non-NULL values.

scenes.headline: See the gap in one query
scenes.voice: Select count star and count phone side by side, and the gap is your missing data.
scenes.caption: Select COUNT(*) and COUNT(phone) side by side, and the gap is your missing data.

scenes.voice: Has count ever fooled you? Comment yes or no.
scenes.caption: Has COUNT ever fooled you? Comment YES or NO.

scenes.voice: Follow K four coding for part eight.
scenes.caption: Follow K4Coding for part 8.

hook.voice: Your report says forty users. The table has fifty. Where did ten go?
hook.headline: Ten users just vanished
